newsitem.title: USA: Gillette earnings aided by Duracell merger.
newsitem.headline: Gillette earnings aided by Duracell merger.

text.p: Gillette Co. Friday reported higher earnings, helped in part by the newly acquired Duracell battery company.

Gillette, which makes razors and other personal care products, said blade and razor sales for the total year and fourth quarter rose well above the prior year's comparable periods, wand profits increased sharply. Duracell products sales for the total year were considerably higher, and profits surpassed those of the year before.
Gillette earned $398.3 million on revenues of $3 billion for the quarter. Excluding merger-related costs of about $283 million, Gillette earned 72 cents a share.
Wall Street analysts had expected Gillette to post income of 63 cents a share, according to estimates compiled by First Call.
In the same period of 1995, Gillette earned $352.4 million, or 64 cents a share, on revenues of $2.72 billion.

For the year, Gillette earned $1.23 billion, or, before merger costs, $2.22 a share. In 1995, it earned $1.07 billion, or $1.94 a share. Revenues rose to $9.69 billion from $8.83 billion a year earlier.

"The combined businesses of Gillette and Duracell will benefit from global sales and distribution synergies, shared technologies important to low-cost manufacturing and new product development, and expanding global brand leadership positions," Alfred M. Zeien, chairman and chief executive officer, said.

Currency exchange losses were higher for the total year and the fourth quarter, but net interest expense and the effective tax rate, before one-time, merger-related costs, were lower in both periods, compared with the year earlier, Gillette said.

Gillette stock closed up 62.5 cents at $81.50 on the New York Stock Exchange. Its results were released after the close of trading and in after-hours over-the-counter trading, its stock traded as high as $83.
